events.objective: Establish symptom onset and blast radius. Query logs/metrics to pin down when order-service POST /v1/orders 500s started, error signature/stack traces, and whether it is truly order-service-only or also affects other services (especially derivatives-related: pricing, market-data, exchange gateway, DB). Pull error-rate/latency/saturation trends from ~11:30Z to 13:59Z and report whether the fault looks local to order-service or downstream.

Inventory every change (deployments and config changes) across ALL services from ~24h before 12:22Z until now, with exact timestamps, and map service dependencies (what order-service depends on, shared components used by derivatives order flow). Flag anything changed close to symptom onset regardless of which service it belongs to.

Given the onset time and error signature from task a and the change list/dependency map from task b, correlate: identify which changes temporally align with onset and sit on order-service's critical path, and check search_historical_incidents for precedent matches to the same error signature or component. Conclude the most likely faulting component and why, plus one alternative.

shared database connection pool saturation causing 500s

events.statement: Deployment dep-5101 to order-service v2.14.0 occurred at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z, 12 minutes before the 12:22Z report; summary 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders', changes 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain' and 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()'; status live, rolled_back_at null.

The only other deployment in the 2026-03-02T12:00Z–2026-03-03T13:59Z window was dep-5088 to portfolio-service v4.2.1 at 2026-03-03T09:36:00Z ('bump grpc 1.62 -> 1.63'), status live, rolled_back_at null — ~2h46m before symptom onset.

The only config change in the window was cfg-2101 on notification-service: key email.batch_size changed 200 -> 250 at 2026-03-03T11:21:00Z by config-bot ('Tune email batching'). No config change touched order-service or any of its dependencies.

order-service (trading, not shared) directly depends on ledger-db (postgres, shared=true), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce); pricing-engine in turn depends on market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache, shared=true), so order-service inherits redis-cache and market-data-service paths. It is called by api-gateway.

ledger-db and redis-cache are shared components: portfolio-service also writes/reads ledger-db and redis-cache, so a change or load from portfolio-service (including its 09:36Z v4.2.1 deploy) could reach order-service through those shared datastores; both are flagged shared=true with owner platform.

Historical precedents returned as leads only (not evidence for this incident): HIST-115 (2025-09-25) order-service 'connection pool misconfiguration' with 'pool exhausted' symptoms, HIST-110 (2026-01-15) 'Slow orders from ledger-db IOPS throttling' involving order-service+ledger-db, HIST-103 (2025-10-21) order failures from external exchange API outage; a separate search returned HIST-113 (2026-01-28) pricing-engine CPU saturation.

Temporal proximity makes dep-5101 the change closest to symptom onset (order-service itself, 12 min before 12:22Z), while dep-5088 (09:36Z) and cfg-2101 (11:21Z) are further from onset and touch services without a direct functional link to the F&O order path.

events.answer: Across all services for the 24h+ window before 12:22Z there were only 3 changes: order-service deploy v2.14.0 at 12:10Z (12 min before the report; new MarginCheckValidator + removal of legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() — matches the derivatives/F&O symptom), portfolio-service deploy dep-5088 v4.2.1 at 09:36Z (grpc bump, live, not rolled back), and a notification-service config change cfg-2101 (email.batch_size 200->250 at 11:21Z, unrelated to orders). order-service depends on ledger-db (shared Postgres), redis-cache (shared, upstream via pricing-engine), kafka (shared queue) and pricing-engine/exchange-gateway/market-data-service over HTTP; ledger-db and redis-cache are shared by portfolio-service, making it a possible cross-service interference path. No change was found on pricing-engine, ledger-db, kafka, market-data-service or exchange-gateway in the window.

events.statement: First order-service ERROR in the window is at 2026-03-03T12:12:31Z: 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) orderType=FNO orderId=9326cc69'. 426 ERROR lines match between 12:12:31Z and 13:58:50Z.

The error signature is a NullPointerException on a null marginProfile, surfacing as the client-facing 500: two dominant patterns cover all 426 errors -- 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:<n>) orderType=FNO' (224) and 'order rejected with <n>: java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account <n>' (202). Both patterns are filtered to orderType=FNO, the derivatives order type.

order-service error_rate shows a step change between the 12:05Z and 12:12Z buckets: 0.20% avg at 12:05:00Z, then 18.49% at 12:12:00Z, and it stays elevated (17.93-18.97% avg) in every bucket through 13:57:00Z. Baseline 11:30-12:05Z was 0.18-0.27% avg.

market-data-service error_rate stayed at baseline across the whole window: min 0.1%, max 0.32%, mean 0.21%, and the 12:12Z bucket was 0.22% (vs order-service's simultaneous 18.49%). No elevation during the incident.

exchange-gateway error_rate also stayed flat at baseline: min 0.1%, max 0.32%, mean 0.21%; the 12:12Z bucket was 0.17% and every bucket 11:30-13:57Z is within 0.16-0.26% avg. (exchange-gateway also exposes upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency_ms, which were not queried.)

Neither derivatives-adjacent peer shows the order-service symptom: pricing-engine error_rate is flat (min 0.1%, max 0.32%, mean 0.22%, 12:12Z bucket 0.19%) and portfolio-service error_rate is flat (min 0.1%, max 0.32%, mean 0.21%, 12:12Z bucket 0.22%). Both remain at ~0.2% for the entire incident.

events.answer: order-service POST /v1/orders began returning HTTP 500s at 2026-03-03T12:12:31Z, jumping from ~0.2% to ~18.4% error rate and staying flat-high (~18-19%) through 13:59Z. The signature is a NullPointerException inside order-service's own MarginCheckValidator.validate (marginProfile is null), only on orderType=FNO (derivatives) orders. Every peer service checked (market-data-service, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, portfolio-service) shows flat ~0.2% error rate across the same window, so the symptom is currently scoped to order-service, not a broad downstream failure.

events.statement: order-service deployment dep-5101 to v2.14.0 landed at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z, 2 minutes before the first 500 hitting POST /v1/orders at 12:12:31Z; it is the only deployment in the 11:00-14:00Z window and its summary matches the failure mode exactly: 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders', changes 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain' + 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()'. Status is still 'live' with rolled_back_at null.

The NPE stack trace is inside the exact class the deploy introduced: T1/F8-9 report 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88)' with 'marginProfile is null', filtered to orderType=FNO. So the faulting code path is the newly deployed validator, not a pre-existing path.

No config change touched order-service or any dependency in the 11:00-14:00Z window: the only change is cfg-2101 on notification-service (email.batch_size 200->250 at 11:21Z), which has no functional link to the F&O order path.

Historically, no precedent matches the NPE/null-marginProfile signature. The closest order-service precedents are HIST-115 connection-pool exhaustion, HIST-110 ledger-db IOPS throttling (both latency/resource signatures, not null-pointer validation errors) and HIST-103 external exchange outage (504/timeouts). None involves a null field from a validation refactor.

Alternative candidate dep-5088 (portfolio-service v4.2.1, grpc 1.62->1.63) at 2026-03-03T09:36:00Z is 2h36m before onset and touches only a gRPC version; portfolio-service error_rate stayed flat (~0.2%) throughout, and it can only reach order-service indirectly via the shared ledger-db/redis-cache. Its temporal and architectural distance makes it a much weaker fit than dep-5101.

order-service inherits shared upstream paths through ledger-db (shared=true), redis-cache (shared=true, via pricing-engine), kafka and market-data-service — so a shared-component fault could in principle produce the symptom; but all four derivatives-adjacent peers stayed at flat ~0.2% error rate in the same window, which argues against a shared-datastore causation here.

events.answer: Most likely faulting component: the order-service deployment dep-5101 to v2.14.0 at 12:10:00Z — 2 min before onset and it introduced the exact class (MarginCheckValidator) whose NPE on null marginProfile is the error signature; the failure is scoped to FNO (derivatives) orders, matching the deploy's stated scope 'add margin check for F&O orders'. No config change or dependency change aligns. Alternative: a shared-datastore fault from portfolio-service's dep-5088 (09:36Z) reaching order-service via shared ledger-db/redis-cache — weaker because it is 2h36m earlier and all peers stayed at baseline.

events.title: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) introduced a null-marginProfile NPE in the new F&O margin validation path
Null marginProfile originates from an upstream data source (portfolio-service / ledger-db), and the new validator merely surfaces pre-existing bad data
Shared datastore/middleware (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka) degraded at onset, causing order-service failures over a shared path
Adjacent service change (cfg-2101 on notification-service / other adjacent change) rejecting derivative orders

events.summary: H1 is well grounded: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z) predates the first 500 by 2 minutes (12:12:31Z), introduced the exact class in the faulting stack frame (MarginCheckValidator.validate, NPE 'marginProfile is null'), and its stated scope ('add margin check for F&O orders') matches the observed blast radius exactly (all 426 errors filtered to orderType=FNO; error_rate step 0.20%->18.49% at 12:12Z). The competing origins are actively contradicted rather than merely dismissed: dep-5088 is 2h36m earlier and touches only a gRPC version; no config change touched order-service or its dependencies; and all four derivatives-adjacent peers (market-data, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, portfolio-service) stayed at flat ~0.2% error_rate through 13:59Z, which falsifies H3's shared-infrastructure path and removes the mechanism H2 requires to reach order-service. Critically, H1's mechanism is LOCAL (an unguarded dereference of an in-process field on a newly added code path), so it does not require a data corruption to originate anywhere: H2 reduces to 'the new code lacks a null guard', which is H1's trigger, not a competing origin. The same local mechanism is incompatible with H3's connection/timeout error shape. Residual uncertainty concerns only secondary details (the exact reason marginProfile is null, whether latency/pool metrics moved, and the content of the truncated log sample), none of which would change the ranked origin or the fix. Data sources were not down and the one tool failure (pricing-service metric, not_found) is immaterial. Confidence is capped at 0.85 rather than 0.88 to reflect the unexecuted narrow-window config/feature-flag confirmation and the missing resource-saturation cross-check, and to leave room for the rollback confirmation the reasoner itself flagged.

tasks.objective: Establish symptom onset and blast radius. Query logs/metrics to pin down when order-service POST /v1/orders 500s started, error signature/stack traces, and whether it is truly order-service-only or also affects other services (especially derivatives-related: pricing, market-data, exchange gateway, DB). Pull error-rate/latency/saturation trends from ~11:30Z to 13:59Z and report whether the fault looks local to order-service or downstream.
tasks.answer: order-service POST /v1/orders began returning HTTP 500s at 2026-03-03T12:12:31Z, jumping from ~0.2% to ~18.4% error rate and staying flat-high (~18-19%) through 13:59Z. The signature is a NullPointerException inside order-service's own MarginCheckValidator.validate (marginProfile is null), only on orderType=FNO (derivatives) orders. Every peer service checked (market-data-service, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, portfolio-service) shows flat ~0.2% error rate across the same window, so the symptom is currently scoped to order-service, not a broad downstream failure.

tasks.objective: Inventory every change (deployments and config changes) across ALL services from ~24h before 12:22Z until now, with exact timestamps, and map service dependencies (what order-service depends on, shared components used by derivatives order flow). Flag anything changed close to symptom onset regardless of which service it belongs to.
tasks.answer: Across all services for the 24h+ window before 12:22Z there were only 3 changes: order-service deploy v2.14.0 at 12:10Z (12 min before the report; new MarginCheckValidator + removal of legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() — matches the derivatives/F&O symptom), portfolio-service deploy dep-5088 v4.2.1 at 09:36Z (grpc bump, live, not rolled back), and a notification-service config change cfg-2101 (email.batch_size 200->250 at 11:21Z, unrelated to orders). order-service depends on ledger-db (shared Postgres), redis-cache (shared, upstream via pricing-engine), kafka (shared queue) and pricing-engine/exchange-gateway/market-data-service over HTTP; ledger-db and redis-cache are shared by portfolio-service, making it a possible cross-service interference path. No change was found on pricing-engine, ledger-db, kafka, market-data-service or exchange-gateway in the window.

tasks.objective: Given the onset time and error signature from task a and the change list/dependency map from task b, correlate: identify which changes temporally align with onset and sit on order-service's critical path, and check search_historical_incidents for precedent matches to the same error signature or component. Conclude the most likely faulting component and why, plus one alternative.
tasks.answer: Most likely faulting component: the order-service deployment dep-5101 to v2.14.0 at 12:10:00Z — 2 min before onset and it introduced the exact class (MarginCheckValidator) whose NPE on null marginProfile is the error signature; the failure is scoped to FNO (derivatives) orders, matching the deploy's stated scope 'add margin check for F&O orders'. No config change or dependency change aligns. Alternative: a shared-datastore fault from portfolio-service's dep-5088 (09:36Z) reaching order-service via shared ledger-db/redis-cache — weaker because it is 2h36m earlier and all peers stayed at baseline.

critiques.summary: H1 is well grounded: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z) predates the first 500 by 2 minutes (12:12:31Z), introduced the exact class in the faulting stack frame (MarginCheckValidator.validate, NPE 'marginProfile is null'), and its stated scope ('add margin check for F&O orders') matches the observed blast radius exactly (all 426 errors filtered to orderType=FNO; error_rate step 0.20%->18.49% at 12:12Z). The competing origins are actively contradicted rather than merely dismissed: dep-5088 is 2h36m earlier and touches only a gRPC version; no config change touched order-service or its dependencies; and all four derivatives-adjacent peers (market-data, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, portfolio-service) stayed at flat ~0.2% error_rate through 13:59Z, which falsifies H3's shared-infrastructure path and removes the mechanism H2 requires to reach order-service. Critically, H1's mechanism is LOCAL (an unguarded dereference of an in-process field on a newly added code path), so it does not require a data corruption to originate anywhere: H2 reduces to 'the new code lacks a null guard', which is H1's trigger, not a competing origin. The same local mechanism is incompatible with H3's connection/timeout error shape. Residual uncertainty concerns only secondary details (the exact reason marginProfile is null, whether latency/pool metrics moved, and the content of the truncated log sample), none of which would change the ranked origin or the fix. Data sources were not down and the one tool failure (pricing-service metric, not_found) is immaterial. Confidence is capped at 0.85 rather than 0.88 to reflect the unexecuted narrow-window config/feature-flag confirmation and the missing resource-saturation cross-check, and to leave room for the rollback confirmation the reasoner itself flagged.

challenges.issue: The surviving hop ('a missing marginProfile flows in from portfolio-service/ledger-db') is marked ASSUMED with no supporting evidence, and the two facts it needs are contradicted: portfolio-service error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% (F13/F16) and dep-5088 landed 2h36m before onset touching only a gRPC version (F2/F18). Even if upstream data were null, H2's remedy is identical to H1's (restore the null guard in the new validator), so it does not name a different origin or fix. Keep active at low weight; do not rank it first.

No telemetry for ledger-db/redis-cache/kafka was retrieved, so this alternative is dismissed partly by inference from incomplete coverage. That said, the dismissal is independently sound: the fault signature is an in-process NullPointerException in a validation frame, not a connection/timeout/retry error, and every shared-path peer is at baseline. A shared-component fault cannot produce this stack trace.

Stated confidence 0.88 exceeds what the evidence fully closes: the 12:05->12:12Z step is not paired with order-service latency/pool/CPU metrics, so a coincident resource-pressure contributor is not formally excluded (though it could not explain a validator NPE); and the change inventory is from a single source, so an unrecorded feature-flag/infra change in the 2 minutes before onset is not excluded.

Depends on F8/F9, whose log result was truncated (40 of 426 matches). Onset time and the two dominant NPE patterns are reliable, but the per-instance/endpoint distribution is not exhaustively confirmed. This does not threaten the origin, only completeness of blast-radius detail.

The mechanism hop 'the new validator is inserted into the validation chain for F&O orders only' is supported only by the deploy summary text (F1/F14), not by code or config inspection; the same summary is the source of both the hypothesis and its scope match, which is a mild circularity. It is not fatal because the observed FNO-only filtering is independent evidence consistent with it.

evidence_requests.rationale: Removal-of-cause is the single strongest available confirmation that the deploy, not coincident data or resource pressure, is the origin. It is an independent test of H1 rather than a restatement of existing evidence.

evidence_requests.question: For order-service, pull latency_p99_ms, request_rate and cpu_pct / db_pool_in_use for 11:30-13:59Z (or from the incident start to now) and report whether any saturation or latency step coincides with the 12:12Z error-rate step.
evidence_requests.rationale: This is the one unclosed alternative mechanism: if error_rate stepped without any latency/pool/cpu movement, resource exhaustion is excluded and the pure code-path explanation for H1 is confirmed; if it moved, the 'coincident resource exhaustion' assumption must be re-examined or the confidence lowered accordingly.
